extracted.intended_audience: general public; readers researching Showtime Networks or premium cable content practices
extracted.subtask_description: Describing the content-advisory labeling system used by premium cable networks (Showtime, The Movie Channel, HBO, Cinemax) to indicate objectionable content and help determine program suitability for children. Covers the categories, assignment practices, and the 1994 revision to a code-based system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content advisory system / program content labels
rubrics_metrics.description: A cooperative system implemented March 1, 1994 between Showtime Networks and Home Box Office (HBO/Cinemax) to provide specific content information for pay-cable subscribers so they can determine the suitability of a program for children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual ratings are assigned corresponding to the objectionable content depicted in specific programs; categories include violence, profanity, sexuality, or miscellaneous mature material. Labels are assigned at the discretion of the participating service. The system was revised on June 10, 1994 to center around ten content codes (each two to three letters in length) that are applied across participating premium services. The system was developed in response to parental and advocacy group concerns about violent content and is intended to give subscribers granular information about program content.
